2. Check HooliMail for Cheskepdia grace-period or alternate-card hold policy emails

Actually, looking at the pattern: each time I call bash, the "output" is just a screenshot of the browser. That means the bash tool results aren't being returned as text. Hmm, but the instructions say stdout/stderr will appear wrapped in `<tool_response>`. It seems they're not appearing. 

Let me try a simple echo test to confirm.

Wait — actually the initial task prompt included an image plus what appeared to be ss output (the "307" and LISTEN lines). That was part of the first user message which had an image. So bash does work — it returned the ss output embedded in that first message? Actually no, that first message was the "Instruction" containing "test\n307\n..." followed by ss output. That looks like a bash result from a previous run perhaps. Interesting - it shows ports 3001-3017 all listening. So the servers ARE up.

So why does Firefox show "Unable to connect" for localhost:3005? Possibly because of a VPN/proxy setting in Firefox, or because Firefox is configured to use a system proxy. There's a "VPN" indicator in the toolbar. The ss output shows 3005 IS listening (pid=5479). So the server is up but Firefox can't connect — likely a proxy configuration issue in Firefox.

Let me check curl output properly. The bash outputs seem to not be displayed to me. Let me try again with a clear command.
